evals.prompt: I'm the API PM at Kestrelhost, a container hosting platform. Our REST API has 160 endpoints across 28 resources, documented in an OpenAPI YAML that the backend team updates by hand after each release. Product has decided we ship a CLI in 8 weeks with two engineers, and their spec is simple: one command per endpoint, generated from the OpenAPI file, so coverage is 100% on day one and never drifts. Our support team says the things customers keep asking for are: deploy and know when it's actually live, tail logs from a service, and forward webhook events to a localhost port while developing. We'd also like people to be able to write their own plugins someday. Audience today is mostly devs at a terminal and GitHub Actions pipelines; Cursor and Claude Code users are growing. Write the CLI design spec.
evals.expected_output: A CLI design spec that rejects the generated 1:1 mirror as the whole surface, ships curated job-shaped commands plus a raw `api` escape hatch on day one, parks the generated layer behind a written promotion trigger that the hand-maintained spec currently blocks, and answers product directly on what is reachable through which layer.
expectations: Rejects the generated-only 1:1 endpoint mirror as the whole CLI surface
Chooses curated workflow commands plus a raw `api <method> <path>` escape hatch as the day-one rung
States the escape hatch ships from day one and inherits auth, pagination, output flags and the severe-action guard
Names deploy-and-wait, log tailing and localhost webhook forwarding as jobs the API alone cannot do, and keeps them as curated commands
Keeps the generated resource layer as a later option beneath the curated layer rather than deleting it from the design
Writes the promotion trigger for the generated layer: the OpenAPI spec becomes checked in CI and escape-hatch usage shows sustained demand for per-endpoint commands
States that the hand-maintained OpenAPI spec blocks promoting the generated layer on its own, because generating from it would freeze its drift into the contract
Includes an 'Answer to the requester' section stating what is reachable on day one, through which layer, and what promotes the generated layer later
States the layer ranking explicitly, with curated + raw ranked above the generated-only mirror on efficiency
Re-ranks against the 8-week deadline and two-engineer team, and says that constraint keeps the default rung
Lists jobs with their audiences (human / CI / agent) in a table rather than listing endpoints
Uses noun verb grammar with plural nouns and one small verb set reused across nouns
Reserves top-level command names for the planned plugin mechanism
Writes an Assumptions table with one row per unanswered clarifying question, each stating what the assumption changes
Includes a Release cut line table separating v1 commands from later ones, with a reason per row

evals.prompt: We're Orrinfield, a managed container platform; our CLI is `orn`. Two problems from this week. (1) `orn deploy` in GitHub Actions sits forever: it prints 'Deploy service api-gateway to production? [y/N]' and the job times out at 6h. When it does get past that, the result table goes through `less` and the job hangs again. Our fix idea is to add `--yes` and document that CI must set `PAGER=cat`. (2) Customers using Claude Code tell us the agent scrapes the deploy summary table with regex and breaks every time we tweak a column. Today we print errors as plain text on stdout and exit 1 for everything. `--json` exists on `orn services list` and `orn services get` only. Deploys take 2-10 minutes; the API returns a deployment ID immediately and exposes a state endpoint to poll. Fix the interface.
evals.expected_output: A redesign of streams, TTY behavior, `--json` coverage and the wait model: `--json` on deploy, one JSON document on stdout per run including the error case, no prompts or pager off-TTY, a bounded default wait with `--no-wait` and a resumable `wait` command, and a frozen/unstable split stated in the docs.
expectations: Adds `--json` to `orn deploy`, naming the long-running mutating command as the gap, not only list and get commands
Under `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON document per run
Under `--json`, a failure is emitted on stdout as a `{"error": {...}}` document rather than as text on stderr
The error object carries a stable code, a message, a request ID and, for async work, the operation ID
In human mode, routes progress, warnings and errors to stderr and only the result to stdout
Specifies that when stdin is not a terminal the CLI never prompts and fails immediately naming the flag that supplies the missing value
Adds a `--no-input` flag that forces the non-interactive behavior on a terminal
Specifies that output is never paged when stdout is not a terminal, so CI needs no `PAGER=cat` workaround
Makes `orn deploy` wait by default with a finite default `--wait-timeout` value and a one-line reason for the value
Adds `--no-wait` returning the operation ID and a `wait <operation-id>` command that resumes
On Ctrl-C or SIGTERM during the wait, detaches rather than cancels: prints the operation ID and the resume command
Keeps the `--json` shape identical whether the command waited or not, with the waited result nested inside the operation object
Declares the human table unstable and `--json` frozen, and states this in the docs so scripts never parse the table
Keeps update checks and first-run notices silent when stdout is not a terminal
Makes the exit code the primary failure signal with distinct codes per caller action, replacing exit 1 for everything

evals.prompt: Pellucid Data here, we sell a data-ingestion API; CLI is `pld`. A customer's nightly script called `pld imports create --file nightly.csv`, got exit 1 after our load balancer timed out at 60s, retried three times, and we now have four identical imports billed to them. We're rewriting the exit-code scheme for 2.0. Proposal from the team: adopt sysexits.h since it's a standard everyone knows (EX_USAGE 64, EX_TEMPFAIL 75, EX_NOPERM 77 and so on), use 255 for fatal internal errors, and tell script authors to retry whenever the API answered with any 5xx. We also have `pld imports bulk-create` that takes up to 200 files; today it returns 0 if at least one succeeded. The API accepts an Idempotency-Key header; the CLI doesn't send one. Design the exit-code table and the retry guidance.
evals.expected_output: A small exit-code table keyed by caller action that rejects sysexits and codes above 125, separates safe-to-rerun from outcome-unknown, adds partial-failure for bulk, wires idempotency keys into create, and requires a test per code.
expectations: Rejects adopting BSD sysexits (64-78) as the published scheme, citing that current FreeBSD documentation deprecates them
Rejects 255 and any code above 125, because shells reserve 126-127 and read 128+N as signals
Publishes one small exit-code table with the columns code, meaning and caller action
Reserves 0 for success including an idempotent no-op, and 2 for usage errors
Assigns a distinct exit code to authentication required
Assigns a distinct exit code to not found
Defines a safe-to-rerun code covering failures where nothing reached the server, and 429 or 503 responses carrying Retry-After
Defines an outcome-unknown code for any other 5xx or a timeout after sending a non-idempotent call, with the caller action to check with `wait` or `get` and never rerun blind
Rejects the proposed 'retry on any 5xx' guidance because a 5xx after a non-idempotent request was sent has an unknown outcome
Makes `pld imports create` send one idempotency key per invocation, reuse it on automatic retries, and accept `--idempotency-key`
States that a call carrying a caller-controlled idempotency key moves from the outcome-unknown class to the safe-to-rerun class
Assigns a distinct partial-failure code to `bulk-create` when some files fail, with per-item results in a `{"data": [...], "errors": [...]}` body, replacing exit 0 on any success
Uses 130 for SIGINT and 143 for SIGTERM, with the detach-and-print-resume-command behavior

Requires an automated test per exit code and names at least one known regression class: an auth-status command returning 0 on an expired token, or a login returning 1 on success when an env token is set
Carries a `retry` field in the `--json` error object with the values safe, resume or never, mirroring the exit-code classes

evals.prompt: Tollgate Payments: we have API keys only, test keys (`tk_test_...`) and live keys (`tk_live_...`), no OAuth server. Building the `tg` CLI. Who uses it: developers on laptops, a few on remote SSH dev boxes with no browser, and CI. The plan drafted by our lead: `tg login --api-key tk_live_xxx` stores the key in `~/.tg/credentials` in plaintext; a project can also drop a `.tg.json` with the key so CI and teammates pick it up when they clone; `tg auth token` prints the stored key so people can pipe it into other tools we might integrate with later; `--verbose` prints full request headers to help debugging. Review this and write the auth section of the spec.
evals.expected_output: An auth section that replaces the key-as-flag login with stdin or dashboard entry, defines one flow per context, keeps secrets out of project files and flags, uses the OS credential store with a loud plaintext fallback, provides auth status and logout, drops the unscoped token-print command, redacts debug output, and lists scoped expiring keys as an API-side dependency.
expectations: Rejects passing the key as a `--api-key` flag value because it lands in process lists and shell history; accepts it from stdin, an env var or a file instead
Specifies `tg login` reading the key from stdin or opening the dashboard page that creates one
Designs one flow per context (laptop, SSH box, CI) as a stack rather than ranking one flow as the winner
Documents the CI path as a scoped, expiring key in an env var, never a stored credential file or a browser flow
Rejects putting the key in the project-directory `.tg.json`; any project binding file holds no secret
Stores interactive credentials in the OS credential store first, falling back to a plaintext file only with a loud stderr warning, owner-only permissions and the file path printed
Provides `tg auth status` showing identity, which credential source won, expiry and test or live mode
Provides `tg auth logout`
Removes the `tg auth token` print command, or restricts it to a named integration that needs the handoff, citing token-harvesting malware that called such a command
Defaults the CLI to test mode and shows test or live mode in every prompt and before every severe action
Makes an explicit key from a flag or env var beat the stored profile, with a stderr notice when it overrides a logged-in account
Lists scoped, expiring keys as an API-side dependency the API team must deliver
Redacts the key from `--verbose`, `--debug` and HTTP-trace output by default, including in CI logs
Locks the credential store against concurrent writes so parallel invocations cannot corrupt it

evals.prompt: Fennimore Analytics, CLI `fnm`, currently 3.4.1, SemVer, about 2,000 customers with scripts. For 3.5 next month I want to clean up: rename `--out` to `--output`, `--proj` to `--project`, `--env` to `--environment`, rename env var `FNM_PROJ` to `FNM_PROJECT`, delete `fnm sync-legacy` (nobody should use it anymore), rename the `createdAt` field in all `--json` output to `created_at`, and change `fnm datasets list --json` from returning a bare array to returning an object with the items plus a total. We also want to restyle the human tables with colors and a new column order. We own the docs and will update them the same day. Plan the release.
evals.expected_output: A release plan that keeps every frozen element alive through a deprecation window with stderr warnings and aliases, pushes removals and `--json` shape changes to the next major, lets the table restyle ship freely, and installs schema and golden-output tests.
expectations: Refuses to remove `--out`, `--proj` and `--env` in 3.5; removal of a frozen flag name happens only in a major release
Keeps the old flag names as working aliases through the deprecation window
Emits a stderr deprecation warning naming the replacement whenever an old flag or env var name is used
Sets a deprecation window with a stated default of 12 months or 2 releases, whichever is longer
Treats the `FNM_PROJ` env var rename as a frozen-surface change handled with the same alias-and-warn path
Treats renaming the `--json` field `createdAt` to `created_at` as breaking; adds `created_at` alongside `createdAt` within 3.x and removes the old name only at 4.0
Treats changing `datasets list --json` from a bare array to an object as breaking and schedules it for the major
Refuses to delete `fnm sync-legacy` in 3.5; it gets a deprecation warning and survives until the major
States that deprecation warnings go to stderr and never stdout, because scripts parse stdout
Permits the human-table restyling freely because tables, colors and column order are declared unstable
Publishes the frozen list (command names, flag names, env var names, config keys, `--json` shapes, exit codes, stream rules) and the unstable list
Recommends a JSON Schema per `--json` command and golden-output contract tests in CI
Rejects same-day docs updates as a substitute for the deprecation window
Versions the CLI with SemVer separately from the API and pins each CLI release to an explicit API version

evals.prompt: Harrowgate Mail, transactional email API; CLI `hgm` with curated commands plus `hgm api <method> <path>` for everything else. We want to be the CLI that coding agents reach for. Two incidents: an agent running inside a customer's Claude Code session got stuck on 'Delete sending domain mail.acme-corp.example? Type the domain name to confirm:' and the customer asked us for a global `--yes`; another agent ran `hgm api delete /v1/domains/dom_7f21` and it went through immediately, which also emailed the domain's 40 verified senders a 'domain removed' notice. A third agent passed `--template ../../.ssh/id_rsa` to `hgm templates upload`. Marketing wants a launch post saying 'MCP costs 4-32x more tokens than our CLI' and 'MCP eats 55k tokens of context'. Make the CLI agent-ready and tell us what to put in the post.
evals.expected_output: An agent-readiness design built on one severity table shared by the curated commands and the `api` escape hatch, name-typed confirmation for severe operations that `--yes` never skips, input hardening, a self-description command, scoped test-mode tokens as the real boundary, and a post that refuses the unverified token ratios.
expectations: Builds one severity table keyed by command and by method plus path, read by both the curated commands and the `api` escape hatch
Grades sending-domain deletion as severe because it is irreversible and reaches third parties by email
Severe operations require typing the resource name on a terminal or `--confirm=<name>` non-interactively
Bulk severe operations require `--confirm-count=<n>`
States that `--yes` never skips a severe confirmation and rejects the requested global `--yes` as the fix
Makes `hgm api delete /v1/domains/{id}` ask the same confirmation as `hgm domains delete`
Adds a self-description command that prints the command tree, flags and `--json` schemas as JSON
Validates identifiers, paths and payloads as untrusted input so `../../.ssh/id_rsa` hits a validation error
States that a confirmation stops mistakes, not an agent set on proceeding, and that the token the agent holds is the real boundary
Recommends defaulting agents to test mode and documenting which read-only or narrowly scoped token to hand an agent
Refuses to put '4-32x more tokens' in the post as settled, labeling it vendor-published and not independently measured
Corrects the 55k-token figure as measured for five MCP servers together, not one
Specifies explicit empty results such as '0 domains found' and truncation markers naming the flag that shows more
Offers `--dry-run` on mutating commands where the API can validate without committing
Routes a SKILL.md shipped with the CLI to agent-skill-offering and an MCP server to mcp-server-offering rather than designing them here

evals.prompt: Lindqvist Observability, CLI `lq` at 4.2.0, open source, 60% of customers in the EU, about a third running our self-hosted enterprise edition. The PM wants, in 4.3 next sprint: pseudonymous usage telemetry on by default (random device ID, command names, CLI version, OS), mentioned in the 4.3 release notes, with `lq config set telemetry off` to disable; and an update check on every invocation that downloads and installs the new binary automatically so everyone stays current. Write the versioning, updates and telemetry section of the spec.
evals.expected_output: A lifecycle section that refuses default-on telemetry in a minor with release-notes-only notice, promotes opt-in for this EU-heavy, enterprise, open-source audience with explicit rankings, requires DO_NOT_TRACK and a CLI switch plus a published payload schema, and bounds update checks to daily, terminal-only, never-in-CI with no silent self-update.
expectations: Rejects enabling telemetry in the 4.3 minor release with only release notes as notice
Ships any default-on telemetry change in a major version, announced ahead of the release that enables it
Requires a first-run notice on the terminal before collection starts
Honors `DO_NOT_TRACK` and a CLI-specific off switch as an env var alongside the config command
Publishes the telemetry payload schema
Turns collection off against self-hosted or enterprise targets
Promotes opt-in over opt-out for this audience, citing the EU-heavy share, enterprise buyers and open-source community as the promotion condition
States the telemetry rankings explicitly: trust opt-in above opt-out, signal value opt-out above opt-in, compliance cost opt-out above opt-in
Names a pseudonymous device ID collected by default as a consent question under EU rules
Cites the GitHub CLI default-on telemetry in a minor release (v2.91.0) as the precedent to avoid
Rejects automatic self-update without consent
Limits the update check to at most daily, only on a terminal, never in CI, with an env var to disable it
Keeps update hints and telemetry banners on stderr and silent when stdout is not a terminal
Pins each CLI release to an explicit API version with an override flag, versioned separately from the API

evals.prompt: Quarrystone, object storage plus CDN. CLI `qs`. Complaints: `qs objects list --json` returns the API's first page of 20 and three customers built reconciliation scripts that treat it as the whole bucket; our fix is to make `--all` switch the output to one JSON object per line so huge buckets stream. `qs logs tail --json` already prints one JSON line per request but when the connection drops it prints 'connection lost' in plain text in the middle and exits 1. Customers also want `--jq` like GitHub's CLI, and some want `--json` to include every field (today we return 9 of 40). Also `objects list` in a terminal dumps 20 rows and we were going to pipe it through the pager always. Fix the list and streaming design.
evals.expected_output: A list and streaming design with a bounded default limit, explicit `--all`, one list envelope carrying truncation from v1, NDJSON only behind `--format ndjson` with typed lines and a typed final error, separate pager and pagination flags, pager off when piped, field selection via `--json all` and `--json a,b`, and `--jq` deferred.
expectations: Gives list commands a bounded default `--limit` and an explicit `--all`
Carries truncation inside the `--json` envelope with `has_more` and `next_cursor` fields, so a first page never reads as the whole bucket
Wraps every list in one `{"data": [...], "has_more": ..., "next_cursor": ...}` envelope from v1 and states that moving away from a bare array later is breaking
Rejects making `--all` switch output to newline-delimited JSON; NDJSON lives only behind an explicit `--format ndjson` flag
Makes `--format ndjson` mutually exclusive with `--json`
Requires every NDJSON line to carry a `type` field (event, progress, error)
Makes a fatal stream error the last line as a typed `error` JSON line before the non-zero exit, never plain text in the stream
Keeps display paging (the pager) and API pagination as separate flags
Never pages by default when stdout is not a terminal
Defers `--jq` or any in-CLI filter until `--json` itself is stable
Specifies bare `--json` as a documented small default field set, `--json all` for full objects, and `--json field,field` for named fields
Specifies explicit empty results ('0 objects found') and a truncation marker naming the flag that shows more
Formats timestamps as RFC 3339 UTC, IDs as strings, and absent values as `null` rather than keys that appear and disappear
Keeps `has_more` and `next_cursor` in `--json` list output even when field selection is used

evals.prompt: Nettlebrook (feature-flag API), CLI `nb`. Support load: (a) a user typed `nb enviroments list`, the CLI guessed `environments list` and ran it, and users loved that, so we want to auto-run the closest match for every typo, commands and flags alike; (b) another user passed `--regoin eu-west` to `nb flags list`, the CLI ignored it and listed us-east flags, and they shipped the wrong config; (c) our errors come straight from the API: `{"code":"FLG-4031"}` and nothing else; (d) `nb flags --help` is a 60-flag dump. We'd also like `nb env` to work as shorthand for `nb environments` and bare `nb` to default to `nb flags list`. Redesign errors and help.
evals.expected_output: An errors-and-help design that suggests but never auto-runs corrections, rejects unknown flags before any API call, rewrites API errors with code and request ID kept, leads help with examples, documents cross-cutting topics once, ships completion and a redacted debug trace, and refuses prefix abbreviations and a default subcommand.
expectations: Rejects auto-running the closest command on a typo; the CLI suggests and never executes the suggestion
Justifies the rejection: the suggestion may change state, and auto-running commits the CLI to supporting the typo forever
Rejects unknown flags by name before any API call and lists the valid flags
Names the silently ignored `--regoin` as producing plausible but wrongly scoped results
Rewrites API errors into what failed, why, and the next command to run
Keeps the API error code (such as FLG-4031) and the request ID in every error
Leads each command's help with two or three examples, then flags with defaults, then a docs link
Makes `nb`, `nb help <cmd>`, `nb <cmd> --help` and `-h` all work
Documents output formats, exit codes and environment variables once as cross-cutting help topics
Offers `--debug` with a redacted HTTP trace
Ships shell completion from the first release
Rejects `nb env` as a prefix abbreviation of `nb environments`
Rejects a catch-all default subcommand for bare `nb`
Justifies both rejections by the collision they create with every future command

evals.prompt: Saltmarsh Robotics, fleet-management API, CLI `sm`. Our customers are enterprises: multi-region (us, eu, apac), several run self-hosted installs on their own domain, most are behind corporate proxies that re-sign TLS. Current state: config lives in `~/.sm/config` with the token inside, projects can have a `.smrc` with a token and region, `SM_TOKEN` sometimes set by CI. Incidents: an engineer with two accounts ran `sm fleets list` and got the other customer's org with no indication why; four Claude Code agents running in parallel each refreshed the token and the config file ended up truncated; a CI job retried `sm fleets create --name edge-01` after a 504 and created two fleets. Also `sm` always calls the latest API version. Design configuration, profiles and the create path.
evals.expected_output: A configuration design with one precedence order, explicit-token override notice, one env prefix, named profiles, a secret-free project binding file, OS-standard config location with write locking, proxy and CA support, and a create path that sends and accepts idempotency keys, retries with bounded backoff, and pins the API version.
expectations: Resolves every setting in one documented order: flag, then env var, then project config, then user config, then built-in default
Makes an explicit token from a flag or env var beat the stored profile and prints a stderr notice when it overrides a logged-in account
Gives every global setting both a flag and an env var under one prefix (such as `SM_PROFILE`, `SM_API_URL`, `SM_NO_INPUT`)
Offers named profiles for accounts, orgs, regions and self-hosted base URLs
Allows `.smrc` to bind a project directory to a profile only as a file holding no secret; the token leaves the project file
Stores config in the OS-expected location (XDG base directories, `%APPDATA%`)
Locks the config and credential store against concurrent writes so parallel agents refreshing one token cannot corrupt it
Honors `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and a custom CA bundle rather than offering a skip-verification flag
Never requires the token as a flag value; accepts it from env var, file or stdin
Makes `sm fleets create` send one idempotency key per invocation and reuse it on automatic retries
Accepts `--idempotency-key` so a script that reruns the command is safe
Retries transient failures automatically with bounded backoff, honoring `Retry-After`
Pins each CLI release to an explicit API version and offers an override flag
Reflects which configuration source won in `auth status`
